div.head: Hu 8
div.ab: Pecoris tinnitum (tintinnum) et canis hoppa et bloþhorn (blauhornum): horum trium singulum est unum solidum ualens; et unumquodque reputatum est (reputatur) melda (id est manifestatio).
Hryðeres belle, hundes hoppe, blæshorn: ðissa ðreora ælc bið anes scill' weorð; ⁊ ælc is melda geteald.

Nola bouis, collarium canis (Anglice dicitur ‘hundes hoppe’, quasi canis circularium, quia hóp: circulus), tuba cornea: horum trium unumquodque ualet unum sol.; et uniuscuiusque modus computatus [melda].
Hryðeres belle, hundes hoppe, blæshorn—ðissa ðreora ælc bið anes scill' weorð; ⁊ ælc is melda geteald.
A cow's bell, a dog's collar and a horn for blowing—each of these shall be worth a shilling, and each is reckoned as an informer.
A cow’s bell, a dog’s collar [?], a blast-horn; each of these three is worth a shilling, and each is reckoned an informer.
Rindes Glocke, Hundes Halsband, Blasehorn: dieser dreier jedes ist 1 Schill. werth; und jedes wird als Anzeiger gerechnet.
An ox's bell, a dog's collar, a blowing-horn: each of these three is worth 1 shilling; and each is reckoned as an informer.

note.label: repeats concern
note.quote: the point about the threefold ordeal repeated a basic concern of Be Blaserum [n. Hu. 8 – 9 (cf. 7:1); Blas. 1]

div.note: ‘⁊’ before ‘hundes’ in B was inserted later. Hk adds a gloss on why the price is so high.
This and the following chapter obviously have no connection with the rest of the ordinance, and are presumably detached statements which the scribe wrongly joined on to this code.
